mainTopic: Practical rules for טבילה: washing the hair and the body's folds, blockers found after immersing, and what a woman may stand on in the מקוה.
overview: This amud gives practical rules for a woman getting ready for טבילה. She should not wash her hair with נתר or sand, and she should wash it with warm water, not cold, because cold water stiffens the hair. רבא teaches that she should rinse the folds of her body. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא that says the water does not need to reach those folds. It answers that the folds must still be places the water could reach, and it compares this to רבי זירא's rule about mixing flour and oil in a מנחה. A story about רבי's maidservant shows that even a bone between the teeth spoils a טבילה. רבא then rules on a blocker found after טבילה, and two versions of his rule are compared. Finally, רב כהנא and רב חנן מנהרדעא argue about why a woman may not stand on earthenware vessels in the מקוה, and a new rule from רב שמואל בר רב יצחק begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No washing hair with natron or sand
steps.stepSummary: A woman preparing for טבילה should not wash her hair with נתר or sand, because each leaves something behind that could block the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: She should not wash her hair with natron or with sand. Not with natron, because it pulls out hair. Not with sand, because it sticks to the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rule about how a woman washes her hair before טבילה: she must not use נתר or sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is a חציצה, something between her body and the water. נתר pulls out hairs that can stay tangled on her head. Sand sticks to the hair. Either one could stay on her during the טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing and combing the hair clean before טבילה

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּחוֹף לֹא בְּנֶתֶר וְלֹא בַּחוֹל;
phrases.english: She may not wash her hair with natron or with sand;
phrases.notes: The start of this sentence, saying who "she" is, comes just before this part of the דף. It is a woman getting ready for טבילה.

phrases.english: not with natron, because it pulls out hair,
and not with sand, because it sticks.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּחוֹף לֹא בְּנֶתֶר וְלֹא בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a series of practical rules about washing the hair before טבילה that began before this part of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not wash the hair with נתר (it pulls out hair) or sand (it sticks), since both can leave a חציצה.

steps.title: Wash hair only with warm water
steps.stepSummary: אמימר quotes רבא: a woman washes her hair only with warm water, not cold water. Water warmed by the sun is also fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רבא: A woman washes her hair only with hot water, not with cold water, and even water warmed by the sun is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new practical rule: hair washing before טבילה must be done with warm water, and sun-warmed water counts as warm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule names one kind of water that works (warm) and one that does not (cold). It also tells us the heat does not have to come from a fire. Water warmed in the sun is good enough.

phrases.english: And Ameimar said in the name of Rava:
A woman washes her hair only with hot water,
but not with cold water,
and even with water heated by the sun.
phrases.notes: This means sun-warmed water is fine too. It does not need to be heated over a fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another rule about hair washing, this time about the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair must be washed with warm water (sun-warmed is fine), not cold.

steps.title: Why not cold water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason cold water is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason cold water is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why cold water does not work. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the rule. It is a simple request for the reason behind it.

phrases.english: Cold water: what is the reason it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why cold water may not be used to wash the hair.

steps.title: Cold water makes the hair stiff
steps.stepSummary: Cold water makes the hair harden, so the hair does not get properly cleaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is cold, and it makes the hair harden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: cold water stiffens the hair, so it does not come clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair washed in cold water stays tight and stiff, so dirt or tangles can stay in it. Warm water softens the hair, so it gets fully cleaned.

phrases.english: Because they are cold and they make the hair harden.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cold water hardens the hair, so it does not get properly cleaned.
steps.whatToRemember: Hair washing before טבילה is done with warm water, not נתר, sand or cold water. Each forbidden option either leaves something in the hair or fails to clean it.

steps.title: Rinse the folds of the body
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a man should always teach his household that a woman rinses the folds of her body with water before טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A man should always teach in his house that a woman should rinse the creases of her body in water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new instruction: before טבילה, a woman should rinse the folded, creased parts of her body with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are places like the armpits, where dirt can collect. רבא wants this to be a regular practice that every household knows about.

keyTerms.meaning: Creased or folded parts of the body

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A person should always teach in his house

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּהֵא אִשָּׁה מְדִיחָה בֵּית קַמְטֵיהּ בְּמַיִם.
phrases.english: that a woman should rinse her creased places in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם יִלְמַד אָדָם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from washing the hair to rinsing the hidden folds of the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman should rinse the folds of her body with water before טבילה.

steps.title: But folds don't need the water at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a ברייתא: creased and hidden places do not need the water to reach them. So why rinse them?
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Creased places and hidden places do not need the water to reach them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule with a ברייתא that seems to make it unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the טבילה is valid even when the water does not touch the folds, then cleaning them seems pointless. Dirt there should not matter, since the water does not have to get there anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden or concealed parts of the body

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Creased places and hidden places
do not need the water to reach them!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that the folds must be rinsed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the water does not need to reach the folds, it makes no sense to require cleaning them.

steps.title: They must be places water could reach
steps.stepSummary: The water does not have to actually reach the folds, but the folds must be places where water could reach. So they must be clean and open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, we do not need the water to actually reach them. But we do need them to be a place fit for the water to reach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating two ideas: water actually reaching a place, and the place being fit for water to reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says the water does not have to touch the folds. It does not say the folds can be blocked. If dirt makes a fold unfit for water, that is a problem. That is why רבא requires rinsing.

keyTerms.meaning: A place that is fit (for something)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up "the water must reach it" with "the water must be able to reach it." The folds need only the second.

phrases.english: Granted that we do not require the water to reach them,
we do require a place that is fit for the water to reach,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: actual contact vs. being fit for contact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since water need not reach the folds, cleaning them seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The folds must still be fit to receive water, so they must be clean.

steps.title: Support from רבי זירא's rule on mixing
steps.stepSummary: The answer matches רבי זירא's rule about a מנחה. If the flour could be mixed with oil, the mixing is not required. But if it could not be mixed at all, the offering is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבי זירא, who said: Whatever is fit for mixing, the mixing does not hold it back. But whatever is not fit for mixing, the mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a general rule from רבי זירא about a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a מנחה, a mixing that was never done does not ruin the offering, as long as the mixing could have been done. If it was impossible to do, the offering is invalid. The same is true for טבילה: water does not have to touch the folds, but it must be possible for it to touch them.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing the flour of a מנחה with oil
Holds back, makes it invalid if missing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's rule: something that does not have to be done must still be possible to do. That is why the folds must be clean, even though the water does not have to reach them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows up in many places: being fit for an action can matter even when the action itself is not required.

phrases.english: in line with Rabbi Zeira,
for Rabbi Zeira said:
Whatever is fit for mixing,
phrases.notes: This is about a מנחה, where the flour is mixed with oil.

phrases.english: the mixing does not make it invalid if it was not done,
and whatever is not fit for mixing,
the mixing does make it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the answer in step 7 in a known general rule.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a place must be fit for water even if the water need not reach it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's rule about mixing the flour and oil of a מנחה.

steps.title: A bone between the teeth of רבי's maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא, quoting רבי יצחק, reports that a bone was found stuck between the teeth of רבי's maidservant after her טבילה, and רבי made her immerse again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: Once, רבי's maidservant immersed and came out, and a bone was found stuck between her teeth. רבי required her to immerse again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story to show how strict the rule about blockers is. Even a hidden place like the inside of the mouth must be free of anything blocking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before taught that hidden places do not need the water to actually reach them, but they must be places where water could reach. The mouth is exactly that kind of place, so a bone between the teeth made the טבילה invalid. רבי ruled she needed a new טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: a maidservant (she also had to immerse to become טהורה)
blocking; something that stands between the body and the water
another immersion; doing the טבילה over again

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the water has to physically wash the inside of the mouth. The point is that the mouth must be a place the water could reach, and the bone blocked that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why women clean their teeth and check their mouths before טבילה.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was an incident with Rabbi's maidservant
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: who immersed and came up out of the water,
and a blocking bone was found on her
between her teeth,
and Rabbi required her to do another immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 7 (hidden places must be reachable by water) to an actual case involving the mouth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blocker even in a hidden place like between the teeth invalidates the טבילה, and she must immerse again.

steps.title: Finding a blocker after immersing: did she wash right before?
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a woman finds a blocker on herself after her טבילה, she does not need to redo it if she immersed right after washing her hair. If not, she must wash and immerse again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If she immersed, came up, and found something blocking on her, then if she immersed right after washing her hair, she does not need to wash and immerse again. If not, she must wash and immerse again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule for a common worry: something blocking is found on the woman after she has already come out of the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the item was there during the טבילה or stuck to her afterward. If she washed her hair just before immersing, she was clean then, so we assume it came afterward. If time passed between washing and טבילה, it may already have been on her, so she must redo the whole process.

keyTerms.meaning: washing and combing the hair clean before טבילה
close to; right before or right after
to wash the hair and to immerse (doing both again)

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If she immersed and came up,
and a blocking item was found on her,
if she immersed right after washing her hair,
she does not need to wash and immerse again,
and if not,
she must wash and immerse again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: טָבְלָה וְעָלְתָה, וְנִמְצָא עָלֶיהָ דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a blocker definitely present during טבילה (Step 9) to a blocker found afterward, where it is unclear whether it was there during the טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blocker found after טבילה does not invalidate it if she immersed right after washing her hair. Otherwise she must wash and immerse again.

steps.title: Second version of רבא: washing on the same day
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רבא's rule says the key is whether she washed on the same day she immersed, not whether she washed right before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: If she immersed on the same day that she washed, she does not need to wash and immerse again. If not, she must wash and immerse again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבא said. The rule is the same, but the time limit is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version she is protected only if the washing was right before the טבילה. In this version it is enough that the washing and the טבילה happened on the same day, even with some time in between.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
If she immersed on the same day that she washed her hair,
she does not need to wash and immerse again,
and if not,
she must wash and immerse again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אִם בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם שֶׁחָפְפָה טָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's rule from Step 10, changing the time limit from 'right before' to 'same day'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blocker found after טבילה does not require a new טבילה if she washed on the same day as the טבילה.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking when the two versions would actually rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions sound close to each other, so the גמרא wants to find a real case where they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them? (in practice)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions given in Steps 10 and 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two versions of רבא's rule give different results.

steps.title: The two cases where the versions differ
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ when she washes on the same day but not right before the טבילה, and when she washes during the day and immerses at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is about immersing close to the washing, and about washing during the day and immersing at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by giving two cases where the two versions of רבא would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case 1: She washed earlier in the day and immersed later that same day. The first version requires the טבילה right after the washing, so it is not enough, but the second version accepts it. Case 2: She washed during the day and immersed that night, right afterward. The first version accepts it because it was close, but under the second version the night may not count as 'the same day'.

keyTerms.meaning: to put right next to (to immerse right after washing)

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of רבא: (1) she must immerse right after washing; (2) she must immerse on the same day as washing. Either way, if she did, a blocker found later does not require a new טבילה. The versions differ on 'same day but not right after' and on 'washed by day, immersed at night'.
steps.confusionAlert: Remember that in הלכה the night starts a new day. That is why washing by day and immersing that night can be 'close' but still not 'the same day'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why women try to wash and immerse close together and with no long break between them.

phrases.english: The difference between them is
about having the immersion right after the washing,
phrases.notes: Under the first version she must do this. Under the second, the same day is enough.

phrases.english: and about washing during the day
and immersing at night.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The versions differ in two cases: (1) washing on the same day but not right before the טבילה, which works only under the second version; (2) washing by day and immersing that night right after, which works under the first version but may not count as the same day under the second.

steps.title: No standing on earthenware vessels while immersing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a woman may not stand on top of earthenware vessels in the מקוה and immerse that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A woman should not stand on top of an earthenware vessel and immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבא about how a woman stands during her טבילה. She may not stand on earthenware vessels that are sitting in the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with blockages on the woman's body. Now the topic moves to what she stands on in the water. רבא gives the rule but not the reason, and the next steps argue about what that reason is.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since רבא gives no reason, the reason we choose decides whether the rule also covers other surfaces, like a wooden plank.

phrases.english: Rava said: A woman may not stand
on top of earthenware vessels and immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִשָּׁה לֹא תַּעֲמוֹד עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי חֶרֶס וְתִטְבּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about טבילה, moving from blockages on the body to what the woman stands on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not stand on earthenware vessels in the מקוה while she immerses.

steps.title: רב כהנא's reason: a decree because of bathhouses
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא thinks רבא's rule is a גזירה so people won't confuse a מקוה with a bathhouse. So he concludes that standing on a wooden plank would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא thought: What is the reason? It is a decree because of bathhouses. That means standing on a wooden plank is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains why רבא forbade standing on earthenware vessels. From that reason he draws a leniency: a wooden plank is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב כהנא's view, the problem is not the act of standing on something. The problem is that it looks like bathing in a bathhouse. Since a wooden plank does not give that impression, it would be permitted. The word סבר ("he thought") hints that this view is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the חכמים
It is fine, it is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: סָבַר ... לְמֵימַר means "he thought to say." In the גמרא this usually introduces an idea that will be rejected right away, and that is what happens in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana thought to say:
What is the reason?
Because of a decree on account of bathhouses,
phrases.notes: Standing on vessels looks like bathing in a bathhouse, whose water is not valid for a מקוה.

phrases.english: which implies that on top of a wooden plank,
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב כָּהֲנָא לְמֵימַר: טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for רבא's rule and draws a leniency from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule is a גזירה because of bathhouses, so a wooden plank is permitted.

steps.title: רב חנן's reason: she will be afraid
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן מנהרדעא rejects רב כהנא's reason. He says the problem is that she will be afraid of falling, and a plank causes the same fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן from נהרדעא said to him: The reason there is that she will be afraid, and on a plank she will also be afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן pushes back on רב כהנא. He gives a different reason for רבא's rule, and that reason also forbids the wooden plank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חנן, the concern is fear: a woman standing on something unsteady will worry about falling and won't immerse properly. A plank is just as unsteady, so רב כהנא's leniency falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: The accepted reason is fear, which stops her from immersing properly, not a decree about bathhouses. So standing on a wooden plank is forbidden too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the reason behind a rule controls how far it reaches. A different reason gives a different result for the plank.

phrases.english: Rav Chanan from Nehardea said to him:
There, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: "There" means רבא's case of the earthenware vessels.

phrases.english: Because she is afraid,
phrases.notes: She worries she will fall, so she won't immerse properly.

phrases.english: on a plank too, she is afraid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא: הָתָם טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב כהנא's reason and the leniency he drew from it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both רב כהנא's reason (a bathhouse decree) and his conclusion that a plank is allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The real reason is fear of falling. That fear exists on a plank as well, so the plank cannot be allowed.

steps.title: A new rule begins: when a woman may not immerse
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק begins a new rule about a case in which a woman may not immerse. The rest of his words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: A woman may not immerse...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next rule. We hear only the opening words, and the details of the case come in what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another practical rule about how a woman must do her טבילה, like רבא's rule. Right now we know only that something will prevent her from immersing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
A woman may not immerse

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: אִשָּׁה לֹא תִּטְבּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new rule about טבילה after the discussion of רבא's rule is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not immerse in a certain situation (the details continue in the following text).
